edit.description: headingSection: skip fenced spans, so only a real heading starts or bounds a section

summary: headingSection reads a fenced `# ...` line as a heading: a cited section truncates at it, and fenced text resolves as a section of its own
acceptance: A `#`-prefixed line inside a fenced code block neither bounds nor starts a section; the per gate and the build prompt both see the whole cited section.
tests: a heading-shaped line inside a fenced block does not bound the cited section
a heading-shaped line inside a fenced block resolves no section of its own
notes: Verified on disk at harness/citeResolver.ts:121-138 (headingSection). A cite over a section carrying a ```sh fence whose first line is `# a shell comment` returns ok:true with text cut at the opening fence; a cite naming that comment line returns ok:true over the fence body. Latent in this repo today — no fenced `#` lines in spec/ or .claude/rules/ — so no shipped cite is wrong yet.
